span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PHYSICAL SYSTEM IS RE-DESCRIBED AS A COMPUTER, AND THE RE-DESCRIPTION IS MARKED AS ONE: Quotation withheld, with unitary transformations performed BY MOVING THE EXCITATIONS AROUND EACH OTHER and measurements BY JOINING EXCITATIONS IN PAIRS. `Can be considered as` is a way of regarding, not an identity, and the whole paper rests on it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PROPERTY IS LOCATED IN THE PHYSICS RATHER THAN IN THE PROTOCOL: such computation is said to be FAULT-TOLERANT BY ITS PHYSICAL NATURE - so what is elsewhere achieved by a procedure is here claimed as a feature of the material. The same word, fault-tolerance, is being attached to a different kind of thing
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PHYSICAL PROCESS IS RE-DESCRIBED AS AN ALGORITHM AND THE HEDGE IS LEFT IN: the spins' mutual interaction forcing a flipped spin back is said to be QUITE SIMILAR TO THE STANDARD ERROR CORRECTION PROCEDURE FOR THE REPETITION CODE, after which - WE MAY SAY THAT ERRORS ARE BEING CORRECTED AT THE PHYSICAL LEVEL. The identification is offered as a manner of speaking
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE ARGUMENT PROCEEDS BY ASKING WHY AN EXISTING PRACTICE IS UNNECESSARY: classical computation CAN ALSO be performed fault-tolerantly, HOWEVER IT IS RARELY DONE IN PRACTICE BECAUSE CLASSICAL GATES ARE RELIABLE ENOUGH - and the next sentence is WHY IS IT POSSIBLE. The paper's question is generated by noticing that a technique is available and unused
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE EXPLANATION IS SOUGHT IN THE EASIEST CASE FIRST AND THE CHOICE IS ANNOUNCED: LET US TRY TO UNDERSTAND THE EASIEST THING - why classical information can be stored reliably on magnetic media - before the quantum case is attempted. The order of explanation is stated rather than left implicit, and the chosen starting point is a fact about ordinary technology
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A THRESHOLD IS REPORTED AS THE OBSTACLE, AND ITS SIZE IS WHAT MATTERS RATHER THAN ITS EXISTENCE: an arbitrary circuit CAN be simulated with imperfect gates PROVIDED they are close to ideal up to a constant precision - and UNFORTUNATELY THE THRESHOLD VALUE IS RATHER SMALL, IT IS VERY DIFFICULT TO ACHIEVE THIS PRECISION. The theoretical solution is granted and then declared impractical by a number
span.note: about this quote: The span contains `small1;` - a footnote marker glued to the preceding word by the extraction. The quote is an exact substring and anchors correctly.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PROBLEM IS DECLARED SOLVED FROM ONE STANDPOINT AND OPEN FROM ANOTHER, WITH BOTH NAMED: physical realization is A BIG CHALLENGE and decoherence is one important problem - but FROM THE PURELY THEORETICAL POINT OF VIEW, THIS PROBLEM HAS BEEN SOLVED. Solved and unsolved at once, distinguished by which standpoint the word is being used from
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AN EXPLICIT CAUTION AGAINST CONFLATING TWO THINGS THE SAME MATHEMATICS DESCRIBES: the local operators SHOULD NOT BE INTERPRETED AS symmetry transformations - the true symmetry transformations are a different set, and MATHEMATICALLY THEY ARE DESCRIBED BY THE SAME ALGEBRA, BUT THEIR ACTION ON PHYSICAL STATES IS DIFFERENT. One formalism, two referents, and the paper stops to say so
span.note: about this quote: DAMAGE SHAPE 5 INSIDE THIS SPAN, and it removes a name. The sentence reads "described by the same algebra , but their action on physical states is different" - with a space before the comma where the algebra's symbol should be. The symbol was displaced past the end of the sentence by the extraction: "...is different. D 15 a b Figure 7:". So the quote says "the same algebra [ ]" and the algebra it names is unrecoverable from the span. The tag does not name it. Found by reading; no guard sees this.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A TERM OF ART IS CONCEDED AND THEN SET ASIDE AS NOT THE RELEVANT PROPERTY: ONE MAY SAY that these codes have QUITE POOR PARAMETERS, and WELL, THEY ARE NOT GOOD CODES IN THE SENSE OF a cited definition - HOWEVER the code corrects almost any multiple error of a stated size, SO THESE CODES WORK. The established criterion is granted, and then shown not to be the criterion that matters here
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: what this limits: the abelian toric-code memory as a usable memory: UNFORTUNATELY, I DO NOT KNOW ANY WAY THIS QUANTUM INFORMATION CAN GET IN OR OUT

span.label: No general theory underlies the constructions given.

span.label: The universal-computation results are stated without full derivation, to appear elsewhere.
span.note: what this limits: the universal-computation results as presented here: (THIS SECTION SHOULD BE CONSIDERED AS AN ABSTRACT OF RESULTS TO BE PRESENTED ELSEWHERE)

span.label: The number the whole fault-tolerance argument depends on is declared unknown in a footnote, with estimates three orders of magnitude apart.
span.note: what this limits: any use of the fault-tolerance threshold cited here: a footnote states the threshold is not known and that published estimates vary across several orders of magnitude
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The case that errors can be corrected by physics rather than by procedure is made by analogy with magnetic storage, and hedged.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that this scheme corrects errors at the physical level: the supporting argument is an analogy with spins on magnetic media, which the author introduces with 'we may say'
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The protection is degeneracy of a ground state on a surface, so the quantity protected depends on the topology chosen.
span.note: what this limits: the amount of protected quantum information claimed here: the protected space is the ground state of the Hamiltonian and is 4g-fold degenerate, where g is the genus of the surface the lattice is placed on
